t.7.12.1: Then the lord of the Rākṣasas, having been consecrated and accompanied by his two brothers, thought about the giving in marriage of his sister, the Rākṣasī.
t.7.12.2: He gave that Rākṣasī, his sister named Śūrpaṇakhā, to the Kālakeya, the lord of the Dānavas, Vidyujjihva by name.
t.7.12.3: Then, having given away his sister, the king, while roaming about on a hunt, saw there, O Rāma, Maya by name, the son of Diti.
t.7.12.4: Seeing him with a maiden as his companion, Daśagrīva, the night-roamer, asked: “Who are you, alone in this forest empty of men and beasts?”
t.7.12.5: Then, O Rāma, Maya said to that night-wanderer who was questioning him: “Listen, I shall tell you all of this, just as it happened to me.”
t.7.12.6: There is an Apsaras named Hemā, dear son, of whom you may have heard before; she was given to me by the gods, just as Paulomī was given to Śatakratu.
t.7.12.8: And for the sake of that Hemā, I then fashioned by my magic power this entire golden city, variegated with diamonds and lapis lazuli.
t.7.12.7: My heart was attached to her, dear one, for five hundred years; and she, on the business of the gods, has gone away, and this is now the fourteenth year.
t.7.12.9: Finding no joy there, bereft of her and deeply grieved, I took my daughter and came from that city to the forest.
t.7.12.10: This is my daughter, O king, who grew in her womb. Together with her, I have come to seek a husband for her.
t.7.12.11: Being the father of a daughter is indeed a sorrow for men who cherish their honor, for a daughter always remains, having placed two families in uncertainty.
t.7.12.12: Two sons were born to me of this wife, dear son: Māyāvī was the first, and Dundubhi came after him.
t.7.12.13: All this has been told to you truthfully, since you asked. Now, my dear, how am I to know you? Who are you, sir?
t.7.12.15: Knowing him to be the son of a brahmarṣi, Maya was filled with joy, and there he resolved to give his daughter to him.
t.7.12.14: Thus addressed, the lord of the rākṣasas courteously spoke these words: "I am the son of Paulastya, and Daśagrīva by name."
t.7.12.16: Laughing, the lord of the Daityas spoke these words to the lord of the Rākṣasas: "This is my daughter, O king, borne by the Apsaras Hemā, a maiden named Mandodarī; let her be accepted as your wife."
t.7.12.17: "Very well," Daśagrīva replied to him, O Rāma, and kindling a fire right there, he took her hand in marriage.
t.7.12.18: For Maya, O Rāma, did not know of the curse laid on him by the ascetic. Knowing that his lineage descended from the Grandfather, Maya gave her to him.
t.7.12.20: Having thus taken a wife, the mighty lord, master of Laṅkā, went to the city and brought home two wives for his two brothers.
t.7.12.19: And he also gave him a most wondrous, unfailing spear, obtained through supreme austerity, with which he struck down Lakṣmaṇa.
t.7.12.22: Vibhīṣaṇa, knower of dharma, obtained as his wife Saramā by name, the daughter of the great-souled Śailūṣa, king of the Gandharvas.
t.7.12.21: Rāvaṇa brought the daughter's daughter of Vairocana, Vajrajvālā by name, and gave her in marriage as the wife of Kumbhakarṇa.
t.7.12.23: She was born on the shore of the lake Mānasa, and, my dear, the lake Mānasa swelled at the coming of the rain clouds.
t.7.12.25: Thus, having taken wives, those Rākṣasas sported there, each with his own wife, like Gandharvas in Nandana.
t.7.12.24: Out of affection, the mother of that girl cried out the words, “Lake, do not rise!” And so she came to be called Saramā.
t.7.12.26: Then Mandodarī gave birth to a son, Meghanāda; he is the one who is called by you by the name Indrajit.
t.7.12.27: For long ago, as soon as he was born, that son of the Rākṣasa, crying, let forth a mighty roar like that of a rain-cloud.
t.7.12.28: When Laṅkā had been stunned into stillness by that roar of his, his father himself gave him the name Meghanāda.
t.7.12.29: Then, O Rāma, he grew up in the splendid inner apartments of Rāvaṇa, guarded by excellent women, like a fire covered over with logs of wood.
